task: Write a formal execution plan for adding a Lattice LLM usage ledger.
outcome: User can open docs/requirements/decisions/lattice-llm-usage-ledger-execution-plan.md and see a concrete, executable plan that explains what to build, what not to claim, how to validate provider-reported token usage, and how local Non-authority differs from Authority receipt-backed proof.
facts: Current Lattice can estimate prompt/template size but does not expose exact provider billing tokens for all host/subagent work.
Existing provider execution records digests, bytes, duration, attempts, and model metadata, but not token usage.
Existing budget-meter can consume tokensUsed or costUnits when provider step summaries include them.
Host Overflow documentation requires execution hosts to remain non-authority and keep receiptVerified=false and productionDone=false unless Authority proof exists.
The requested task is document-only; CLI implementation is out of scope for this story.
constraints: Do not optimize for the sake of optimization.
Only fix or plan for real correctness issues.
Follow consistency of logic across CLI local evidence and Authority Server proof boundaries.
Do not save raw prompts or raw transcripts in a usage ledger.
Do not claim true token usage where the provider did not report usage.
